A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAGELLAN method and Little-Zoo study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–D are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original competence-estimation, reinforcement-learning, generalization, adaptation, and architectural-ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains the original Little-Zoo experiments and adds original competence-estimation simulations using mathematical and BabyAI-Text goals, including language-model comparisons.

M1.justification: The competence estimator, binary cross-entropy objective, experience and weight buffers, absolute-learning-progress calculation, goal-selection procedure, and separate LoRA adapters remain unchanged. The additional language models are experimental variants of the existing method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates Little-Zoo only. v3 adds simulated competence estimation using OpenR1-Math-220k goals in Algebra, Geometry, and Number Theory, and BabyAI-Text goals covering five navigation, manipulation, and compositional task categories. This substantially broadens the represented domains, although actual agent learning is simulated in these additions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained Little-Zoo experiments is unchanged. The added simulations reuse Online-ALP; the Flan-T5 and Qwen variants are MAGELLAN configurations for an ablation, rather than new baseline methods.

E3.justification: v3 adds a distinct evaluation design comparing competence estimates against known success-probability trajectories of simulated learners, with curves spanning approximately 20,000 episodes. It also evaluates Flan-T5-small, Flan-T5-base, and Qwen2.5-0.5B. These are additional protocols; the existing Little-Zoo training budgets, evaluation procedures, and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.2.3 tests sensitivity to the language-model backbone across the mathematical and BabyAI-Text simulations. This adds a focused robustness analysis to the retained architectural ablations, sampling analyses, embedding studies, and adaptation tests.

E5.justification: The retained experiments preserve their eight-seed reporting, means and standard deviations, and mastery-significance threshold. The added simulation figures provide no experiment-specific run counts, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests; no existing statistical reporting is revised.

E6.justification: New Figures 4 and 15 report closer tracking of simulated competence by MAGELLAN than Online-ALP on mathematical and BabyAI-Text goals. Figures 16–17 report similar tracking across the three tested backbones. Existing Little-Zoo results are retained, including MAGELLAN’s Table 2 mean estimation error of 0.11 ± 0.06; these additions are not same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The formal problem statement, competence and learning-progress definitions, estimator objective, ALP equation, and Appendix D.5.2 sample-efficiency calculation are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or mathematical guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same central claims about efficient competence estimation, curriculum construction, and generalization to unseen or evolving goals. The additional simulations support these existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v3 expands the explanation of expert-group assumptions: impossible goals dilute group competence and obscure learning-progress signals, elaborating v1’s brief failure claim. It also interprets the new backbone results as robustness across lightweight language models. Existing applicability cautions in the Impact Statement remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The listed code location changes from LorisGaven/MAGELLAN to flowersteam/MAGELLAN. Appendix A.1 additionally clarifies environment elements, movement onto elements, and observation descriptions. Existing implementation details, hyperparameter tables, hardware requirements, and compute estimates are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds regret-based unsupervised environment design, citing Dennis et al. (2020) and Jiang et al. (2021), and distinguishes goal sampling from goal generation. References for BabyAI, OpenR1, and Qwen2.5 accompany the new experiments. The broader novelty positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized explanatory expansions, adds two Appendix D.2 subsections, standardizes terminology, and replaces the placeholder running header with MAGELLAN. The overall section organization and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 15–17 add a substantial set of category-specific competence trajectories and backbone-comparison panels, extending the visual evidence beyond Little-Zoo. Tables 1 and 4 replace symbolic efficiency entries with high/low labels, and the existing goal-distribution figure gains a full caption. Earlier graphical results are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The new cross-domain simulations and backbone analysis provide useful additional support for competence estimation beyond Little-Zoo, while clearer baseline and environment explanations improve assessability. The gain is limited because these additions simulate learning rather than demonstrate curriculum benefits in new environments, and their simulation construction and uncertainty reporting remain sparse. The core method and established results are preserved.
